title: Colleagues
hook: faith at work mostly looks like honesty and kindness
tomorrow: a stranger at the counter needs time you don't have. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two ways to read neighbor, the whole world and the house next door, and a name to start with: the literal neighbor. Today, the people on the next shift, or the next desk.
screen: `THE LITERAL NEIGHBOR.` → `THE NEXT SHIFT, THE NEXT DESK.`

segments.voice: The hiss of a milk steamer. A printer jamming again. Keys clicking in an office before anyone's had coffee. A workday is mostly noise, and almost none of it is about God. So what does faith at work sound like when nobody mentions God? Mostly, small honest sentences: that was my mistake. I'll cover your shift. She did that, not me.
screen: `A MILK STEAMER, A JAMMED PRINTER.` → `NOBODY MENTIONS GOD.` → `SMALL HONEST SENTENCES.`

segments.voice: In the Bible, faith at work looks less like a sermon by the coffee machine and more like Daniel's record. His rivals went looking for something to accuse him of, and “they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful.” Paul writes to the church at Thessalonica: “study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands,” so “that ye may walk honestly toward them that are without.” Study to be quiet: make a project of being calm, minding your work, being the colleague people trust with the details. Colossians says whose eyes the work is really for: “And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.” And Ephesians puts honesty plainly: “putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.” Members one of another, like parts of one body. Here's one to repeat tonight: in Daniel's story, the only thing his rivals could think to use against him was the law of his God. At work, quiet faith sounds like small truths: the deadline that will slip, the mistake that was yours, the credit that belongs to someone else. Quiet doesn't mean silent when something's wrong. It means calm, honest and steady.
screen: `NO FAULT, ONLY FAITHFUL.` · `STUDY TO BE QUIET.` · `HEARTILY, AS TO THE LORD.` · `MEMBERS ONE OF ANOTHER.` · then, large: `QUIETLY FAITHFUL.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands palms up and look at them: the cups, keys, tools or keyboards they handled this week. Rub them together slowly until they're warm, then lay them still. If you pray, offer the next day's work through them; if not, just feel the warmth fade.
Colleagues. The people we work beside, who may never hear a word about faith and still meet it in how they're treated.
Keep this one: quietly faithful, which is calm and honest, and never silent about the truth. Day seventeen-nineteen.

screen: `DAY 1719 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 38 OF 70.` → `TOMORROW: A STRANGER NEEDS TIME YOU DON'T HAVE. NOW WHAT?`

howItsDone: Day to day, Christians often live their faith at work without speaking of it: honest work, fair credit, kindness to coworkers; some say a short prayer before a shift or a hard meeting.

chat.says: first café shift. dev messed up an order and told the manager it was me. do i call him out?
options: Tell the truth, calmly, to who needs it. Quietly faithful isn't silent; it's honest.
Stay quiet and take the blame. Faith at work means never making any waves.
Call him out in front of everyone so the whole team knows who's honest.
chat.meaning: Ephesians: speak truth, for we are members one of another. Paul: study to be quiet. Quiet means calm and honest, not hiding the truth.
